summary:
MissionBlocks! is a game about building rockets with blocks that we've developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge, with the challenge being "Space Mission Design Game".

What we have developed is a block-building like game, where you can choose between different types of blocks to use and build your rocket, such as metal, thrusters, etc. But, with that, you have to follow the missions' requirements, for example, "use atleast 10 blocks of metal". After building the rocket, launch it into outer space, where you should complete the mission (can be to reach a certain altitude, get the flag, etc.), and once done, you get coins to buy more components and make another rocket for the next mission!

This addresses many things of the challenge, such as only being able to use very scarce resources (with this, comes logical thinking, to buy and sell blocks), designing a rocket around an actual mission about space, energy consumption and others.

Our project is important because it was designed to get minds to expand creativity and logical thinking, because you can create any design you'd like, as long as it follows the requirements for the mission, and if you have the blocks to make your idea come to life.
details:
Our project works with a mission appearing on the top right, showing requirements. Click around to add blocks, hold R and click to remove a block, use Z/X to change blocks, use S to sell, B to buy, and launch with Space! Then, after launching, the rocket will be in space, and can be controlled with the arrow keys. What goes into measure is altitude, velocity, and energy. You should complete the mission without wasting all of your energy to gain coins and proceed!

The benefits it has is actual thought process to create rockets that really do work, with liquid oxygen + liquid hydrogen being the source of energy, thrusters being what makes the rockets move, metal being the exterior, and others. It also expands creativity, because it's possible to create a bunch of fun designs with limited blocks, and clever ways to engineer a rocket that works accordingly with the mission.

The intended impact of this project is making people have passion for rockets, space and engineering, with this being the beginning of a new journey for these new aircraft designers.

To make it, we've used Penguinmod, a famous tool that is Scratch (https://scratch.mit.edu) but more powerful, with extensions and more blocks such as camera, operators, storage, files, etc.

This project is creative because with it, you can let the imagination flow, and discover the wonders of space. Find smart ways to build rockets that complete the missions, and get to the last mission, where you'll reach the moon!
